description:
We are students from SMK Bandar Kuching No.1, passionate about space and education.

Many children’s space games focus too much on fun and too little on real science. We experienced this ourselves growing up.

That’s why we created MARS: THE LAST FRONTIER — an educational game for ages 7–12 that combines engaging gameplay with accurate scientific knowledge.

We’re not just making another space game. We’re creating a better way for kids to truly discover the universe.
summary:
Mars: The Last Frontier is a strategy and survival game designed for kids ages 7–12 managing a Martian outpost. Many existing space education tools are too simplified, static, or unrealistic, leading to misconceptions. By using authentic NASA data, this game balances accurate information with engaging gameplay to ensure young players learn correct concepts. Players make real decisions about life support, radiation shielding, power budgeting, and food production while navigating mission-critical trade-offs. This approach fosters teamwork, strategic decision-making, and sustainability as players work together to solve complex challenges.
The game revolves around three main aspects: Recruitment, Resource Management and Survival Management.
First, players must recruit suitable people with different skill sets to form a balanced crew.
Furthermore, players must manage limited resources, including food, water and energy, to ensure the survival of the crew.
When unexpected crisis strikes—from sudden radiation spikes to intense dust storms—players must make split-second decisions to keep the mission on track, balancing risk and critical trade-offs.
Through these three aspects, the game promotes teamwork, strategic decision-making and sustainability, highlighting the importance of working together, managing resources wisely and building a better future.
details:
Project Details

1. Game Overview

  • A strategy and survival game about establishing a new civilisation on Mars.
  • Earth is becoming increasingly uninhabitable due to extreme weather and environmental destruction.
  • Players must recruit people with different skills and abilities before departing for Mars.
  • Each recruit has unique statistics and expertise for specific jobs.
  • Players must assign crew members, manage resources, construct shelters and develop sustainable systems.
  • The game revolves around three main aspects: Recruitment, Management, and Survival.
  • Collects data from NASA websites(https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/marsfact.html ,NASA InSight Weather API ,NASA InSight Weather API ,https://pds.nasa.gov/?utm_source=chatgpt.com ,https://pds-geosciences.wustl.edu/missions/mro/crism.htm?utm_source=chatgpt.com ,https://nasa-pds.github.io/pds-api/?utm_source=chatgpt.com )

2. Game Objectives

  • Recruit suitable people with different professions.
  • Maintain essential resources.
  • Ensure the long-term survival of the crew.

3. Recruitment System

  • Recruit people with different professions and abilities before departure.
    • Botanist: Grow crops and produce food. Increases overall crop yields.
    • Engineer: Construct shelters and infrastructure.
    • Unknown: Plays a random role. A jack of all trades, master of none.
    • Mechanic: Maintain machines and equipment. Conserves energy levels with efficiency.
  • Limited recruitment slots require players to select a balanced team.
  • Choose characters with complementary skills and abilities.

4. Landing Locations

  • Players can choose between four landing locations on Mars.
  • Each location provides different starting resources and crop reset rates.

5. Resource Management System

Four Essential Resources

  • Energy
  • Water
  • Oxygen
  • Food

Resource Management Objectives

  • Balance resource production and consumption.
  • Prevent resource shortages.
  • Prioritise essential activities.
  • Maintain sufficient resources for survival.
  • One sol represents one Martian day.

6. Crew Assignment System

  • Assign recruited members to suitable professions after arriving on Mars.
    • Botanists: Farming.
    • Engineers: Construction.
    • Unknown: Plays a random role
    • Mechanics: Equipment maintenance.
  • Assign the right people to the right jobs to improve efficiency.

7. Main Gameplay

RECRUIT

  • Recruit people with different skills.
  • Compare character statistics.
  • Select a balanced team.
  • Prepare for the journey to Mars.

BASE SELECTION

  • Select different bases with different tradeoffs.

MANAGE

  • Monitor energy, water, oxygen and food.
  • Assign crew members to suitable jobs.
  • Control resource consumption.
  • Maintain the population's needs.

8. Winning and Losing Conditions

Winning Conditions

  • Survive for 10 in-game days.
  • Avoid depleting essential resources.
  • Maintain sufficient resources.
  • Ensure the crew's survival.

Losing Conditions

  • Any one of the resources become depleted.
  • No longer sustains its crew’s survival.

9. Educational Values

  • Real Planetary Science: Introduces young learners to authentic facts about Mars, including its atmosphere, surface conditions, and environmental challenges.
  • Space Exploration & Curiosity: Inspires children's interest in STEM fields, space travel, and scientific discovery through engaging, hands-on decision-making.
  • Fact-Based Problem Solving: Teaches resource management, environmental awareness, and critical thinking using accurate scientific concepts and real-world data.

10. Main Message

  • Highlights the consequences of environmental destruction and promotes environmental awareness.
  • Emphasises the importance of sustainable development and responsible resource management.
  • Reminds players that protecting Earth should always remain a priority, even if humanity establishes a new home on Mars.
  • Inspires young minds through accurate space science and authentic planetary data.

Use of AI/SI

We used AI to generate picture ideas, develop game concepts and assist in writing and fixing our code. AI helped us improve our ideas and make the game development process easier. Such as using Claude for back-end of the game, machine-learning, and using Gemini for model training.

Dust Storm Prediction Model (Machine Learning) Model Training

  • Uses an XGBoost machine learning classifier (XGBClassifier) deployed through a FastAPI backend to forecast Martian dust storm risks during Rover Ice-Mining missions.
  • Trained on five Mars Years (MY 28–32) of real satellite observations from the Mars Dust Activity Database (MDAD v1.1).
  • Divides Mars into eight equal latitude bands (from -90° to +90°) and calculates daily dust storm coverage for every Martian sol.
  • Analyzes 26 engineered atmospheric features, including Martian seasonal cycles (solar longitude), current and historical dust levels (1- to 7-sol lags), 7- and 14-sol rolling averages, hemispheric dust trends, and neighboring latitude band activity.
  • Splits data chronologically by Mars Year to prevent data leakage, using MY 31 for validation and threshold tuning before training the final production model on MY 28–31.
  • Predicts whether dust coverage in a latitude band will exceed the 1% storm threshold within the next 3 sols.

Model Accuracy and Performance

  • Achieves 85.5% to 85.7% overall forecast accuracy (with 84.6% balanced accuracy and a 0.873 PR-AUC score) on the completely unseen Mars Year 32 test set, outperforming standard persistence and seasonal climatology baselines.
  • Maintains a consistent 84.8% average accuracy (and 0.890 PR-AUC) across five-year leave-one-year-out cross-validation (MY 28–32).
  • Detects brand-new dust storm formations during clear weather conditions with 85.1% accuracy.
  • Provides reliable multi-day forecasts across 1- to 7-sol horizons, achieving 85.9% accuracy at 1 sol ahead and maintaining 76.3% accuracy up to 7 sols ahead.
